On November 13, 1987, at 11:52 PM, Gérard heard his son screaming in the garage. He cut the power.

The transfer stopped at 61 %. Raymond, wired in as the witness, died in his chair. Gérard walled him in. Then he took out of the machine what hadn't gone across and put it under glass. Every ten years, afraid it would fade, he copied it onto new memory: 640 KB in 1987, 64 GB today. What was left of Léo didn't grow. It's the room it takes up that grew.

What walks the halls is neither Léo nor Raymond. It's what's left when you cut two people into pieces and glue the pieces back together in the dark. It wears the face of one and looks for the father of the other. Since then, it has been filling the gaps with the memory of the whole world, and the whole world has run out of memory.

Gérard never knew if he was keeping his son or keeping him from coming back. He kept the case for thirty-nine years so he wouldn't have to choose.
